Fact.Name: Had student loan interest payments
Fact.Description: Whether the TP or spouse had student loan interest payments

Fact.Name: Student loans qualify
Fact.Description: Whether the TP affirms that their loans qualify for the deduction

Fact.Name: Flow show student loans qualify
Fact.Description: Whether to show the "student loans qualify" screen in the flow. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) line 8c column C: asks the California section 127 question when the federal one was not asked).

Fact.Name: Student loan interest amount
Fact.Description: The amount of interest that the TP affirms that they or their spouse paid on qualifying student loans, not including any amount that is also deductible under another provision of the tax law (for example, home mortgage interest) — IRC 221(e)(1)’s first clause. Interest paid includes voluntary payments made before the loan is otherwise due, until the loan is paid off. The TP must be legally obligated to make the payments: interest on a loan the TP is NOT legally obligated to repay is never deductible, no matter who paid it; conversely, if someone else pays interest on the TP's behalf on a loan the TP IS legally obligated to repay, the TP is treated as receiving and then paying that amount. The figure need not equal Form 1098-E: an institution need only issue that form for $600 or more of interest it received in the year, a loan taken out before September 1, 2004 may have origination fees and capitalized interest omitted from the form's stated-interest figure entirely, and any qualifying interest the TP paid that never appears on the form is still deductible if paid. Where a single payment covers both interest and principal and the tax-purpose allocation differs from the servicer's own statement, a payment applies first to unpaid stated interest, second to allocable loan origination fees, third to unpaid capitalized interest, and only the remainder to principal. Do not include: loan origination fees that pay for property or services the lender provides, such as commitment fees or processing costs; or interest to the extent it was paid through the TP's participation in the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program, a state education loan repayment program eligible for Public Health Service Act funds, or another loan repayment assistance program whose repayments are tax free to the TP. Those program payments are the exception to the paid-by-others rule above: the TP is not treated as having paid that interest. Form 1098-E box 1 (Student loan interest received by lender). California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) line 21 column C).

Fact.Name: Student loan interest paid by employer under section 127
Fact.Description: Screen: shown immediately after the student loan interest amount question, only when /flowShowStudentLoansAmount is true. Question: "How much of the interest you just entered did your employer pay on your behalf, tax-free, under an educational assistance program?" Help text: for payments made after March 27, 2020, don't count interest your employer paid for you under a section 127 educational assistance program toward your deduction — enter $0 if none applied. Unanswered posture: this is a condition of allowance under IRC 221(e)(1) on a return that CLAIMS the deduction (/flowShowStudentLoansAmount true) — leaving it unanswered on a claiming return makes /studentLoanInterestAmountNetOfDoubleBenefit, and the deduction it feeds, Incomplete, not a silent $0-reduction default. Validation: a whole-dollar amount, $0 or more. Feeds /studentLoanInterestAmountNetOfDoubleBenefit. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) line 8c column C section 127 add-back and line 21 column C).

Fact.Name: Student loan interest paid from tax-free QTP earnings
Fact.Description: Screen: shown immediately after /writableStudentLoanInterestEmployerPaidSection127, only when /flowShowStudentLoansAmount is true. Question: "How much of the interest you just entered was paid using tax-free earnings from a 529 (Qualified Tuition Program) distribution made after 2018?" Help text: earnings from a post-2018 QTP distribution that were tax-free because they were used to pay student loan interest can't also count toward this deduction — enter $0 if none applied. Unanswered posture: this is a condition of allowance under IRC 221(e)(1) on a return that CLAIMS the deduction (/flowShowStudentLoansAmount true) — leaving it unanswered on a claiming return makes /studentLoanInterestAmountNetOfDoubleBenefit, and the deduction it feeds, Incomplete, not a silent $0-reduction default. Validation: a whole-dollar amount, $0 or more. Feeds /studentLoanInterestAmountNetOfDoubleBenefit. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540) line 21 column C (529(c)(9) QTP leg)).

Fact.Name: Student loan interest amount, net of the section 221(e)(1) double-benefit reduction
Fact.Description:
/studentLoanInterestAmount reduced, but not below zero, by any employer-paid amount excluded under section 127 (/writableStudentLoanInterestEmployerPaidSection127) and by any tax-free post-2018 QTP-earnings amount under section 529(c)(9) (/writableStudentLoanInterestFromTaxFreeQtpEarnings). Section 221(e)(1) applies both reductions to the subsection (a) amount PRIOR to subsection (b), so this fact stands in place of the raw /studentLoanInterestAmount wherever the 221(b)(1) $2,500 cap or the 221(b)(2) MAGI phaseout is computed.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: the two 221(e)(1) reduction legs are conditions of allowance on a return that has CLAIMED the deduction (/flowShowStudentLoansAmount true — the screen gate both follow-ups are shown behind). On a NON-claiming return the follow-ups are moot and this fact reads /studentLoanInterestAmount unmoved. On a CLAIMING return, both follow-ups must be genuinely answered before a deterministic value resolves; leaving either one unanswered resolves this fact — and /studentLoanInterestAdjustmentAmount downstream — Incomplete, disclosing the return as unfinished rather than silently granting the full, unreduced deduction.

Fact.Name: Forms 1098-E
Fact.Description: Source documents received on Form 1098-E, Student Loan Interest Statement, one item per document (one lender's statement of the interest it received on one borrower's loans). This information-return collection records the document; it is not a second statement of the deduction, which stays /studentLoanInterestAmount. Nothing federal reads it yet; its items are exported for the state returns and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: 1098-E document owner
Fact.Description: The filer to whom this document belongs: the person on this return named as BORROWER on the Form 1098-E. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed, because a spouse's statement would otherwise carry the wrong person.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1098-E belongs to the primary filer. Completeness-first, the shape the sibling document-intake modules carry: an unanswered ../filer resolves complete-safe FALSE rather than inheriting a primary-filer default. Read only by ../borrowerTin.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: The secondary twin of ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, MFJ716-shaped at birth: IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler) is a conjunct, so on a single-filer return an answered ../filer resolves Complete FALSE instead of Incomplete forever. Read only by ../borrowerTin.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E BORROWER'S TIN
Fact.Description: The BORROWER'S TIN box, derived from this document's own borrower (../filer): the primary filer's TIN on the primary filer's Form 1098-E, the secondary filer's on the spouse's, never the return's primary filer by default. The lender may print only the last four digits on Copy B (Instructions for Borrower, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, page 4, LEFT column); this fact is the full number the return already holds. Nothing to ask. Feeds nothing federal; exported for state systems and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E VOID box
Fact.Description: The VOID checkbox in the header of Copy A (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, page 2); the borrower's Copy B does not carry it. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: The CORRECTED checkbox: "CORRECTED" on Copy A, "CORRECTED (if checked)" on the borrower's Copy B (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). Checked means the amounts on this statement replace an earlier one's. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E RECIPIENT'S/LENDER'S name, address and telephone
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S/LENDER'S block: name, street address, city or town, state or province, country, ZIP or foreign postal code, and telephone number, printed as ONE cell and taken as one writable (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). The lender is the recipient of the interest, which is why the form prints both role words. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E RECIPIENT'S TIN
Fact.Description: The RECIPIENT'S TIN box: the lender's identifying number (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). The generator had defaulted this cell to STRUCTURAL; it is a box the lender fills (INPUT-FORMS section e). Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E BORROWER'S name
Fact.Description: The BORROWER'S name box, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). Which person on this return the borrower is stays ../filer, not this box. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E borrower's street address
Fact.Description: The borrower's "Street address (including apt. no.)" box, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E borrower's city, state and ZIP
Fact.Description: The borrower's "City or town, state or province, country, and ZIP or foreign postal code" box, one cell (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E account number
Fact.Description: The "Account number (see instructions)" box (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3): an account or other unique number the lender assigned to distinguish the borrower's account (Instructions for Borrower, same file lines 70-71, RIGHT column); it tells two statements from one lender apart. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E box 1 student loan interest received by lender
Fact.Description: Form 1098-E box 1, "Student loan interest received by lender" on this account (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3; Instructions for Borrower, same file lines 72-78, RIGHT column: for loans made on or after September 1, 2004 it includes loan origination fees and capitalized interest). RECONCILIATION, NOT A REWIRING: the federal deduction reads /studentLoanInterestAmount, the interest the filer affirms PAYING on every qualified loan, which may differ from what lenders report (Pub. 970, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p970.pdf, page 34, LEFT column); that fact is not a sum over this collection, and reconciling the two is a named successor. Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.

Fact.Name: Form 1098-E box 2 box 1 does not include loan origination fees or capitalized interest
Fact.Description: Form 1098-E box 2: "Check if box 1 does not include loan origination fees and/or capitalized interest, and the loan was made before September 1, 2004" on Copy A; Copy B prints "If checked, box 1 does not include loan origination fees and/or capitalized interest for loans made before September 1, 2004" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1098e--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). Checked means the borrower may have deductible origination fees or capitalized interest not shown in box 1 (Instructions for Borrower, same file lines 79-82, RIGHT column; see Pub. 970). Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. Feeds nothing federal; stored for the state returns (several states allow their own student loan interest subtraction from the federal figure) and bound in the Form 1098-E register.
